qc.label_under_test: an adjective naming absurd or comic oddity ('absurd', 'humorous', 'ridiculous', 'silly', 'bizarre'): the word itself, which fires even for a non-funny 'bizarre accident', as against plain or serious adjectives in the same slot

neighbours.label: a silly-comic descriptor (silly, goofy, wacky, ridiculous, funny, absurd) placed as a modifier before a noun or in a list of modifiers; quiet for serious or merely cheerful adjectives and for a bare predicate like 'was really funny'
fire: My nephew wore a silly hat with a propeller on top to the picnic.
The dog made a goofy face every time we opened the treat jar.
She told a long, wacky story about a llama who ran a bakery.
He showed up in a ridiculous costume made entirely of cardboard boxes.
We watched a funny video of a cat falling off the couch.
The play had an absurd plot involving time-traveling penguins.
It was a loud, silly, wonderfully goofy parade through the town square.
Grandpa still does that wacky dance at every family wedding.
quiet: My nephew wore a red hat with a wide brim on top to the picnic.
The dog made a sad face every time we closed the treat jar.
She told a long, serious story about a farmer who ran a bakery.
He showed up in an elegant costume made entirely of black velvet.
We watched that video of a cat falling off the couch, and it was really funny.
The play had a tragic plot involving a family torn apart by war.
It was a loud, cheerful, wonderfully festive parade through the town square.
Grandpa still does that slow, graceful dance at every family wedding.

predictions: 6/8 fire, 0-1 near misses; the 'was really funny' near miss may leak a little
